title: The Africa Pivot: India and Japan’s Quest for Critical Mineral Security
gist: India and Japan are folding Africa's critical minerals into their formal economic-security partnership via a joint declaration, positioning the Indian Ocean as a corridor linking African supply to Asian industry.

insights.claim: Africa holds 55 percent of the world's cobalt, 47.65 percent of manganese, 21.6 percent of graphite and 5.9 percent of copper, making it central to energy-transition supply chains.
insights.speaker: Varuna Shankar
insights.so_what: Cobalt and manganese concentration is the supply-risk lever for battery and steel chains.

insights.claim: The India-Japan Joint Declaration on Economic Security Cooperation places Africa squarely within the two countries' formal partnership architecture, backed by the Joint Economic Forum, a JETRO strategic report and the Asia-Africa Growth Corridor.
insights.speaker: Varuna Shankar
insights.so_what: Expect state-backed Indian and Japanese investment and offtake deals in African minerals, digital infrastructure and green energy.
